candidates.exact_span:
Under the provisions of Part III.D.7.b.(3) of this permit, violations of daily maximum limitations
for the following pollutants shall be reported orally to EPA Region 6, Compliance and Assurance
Division, Water Enforcement Branch (6EN-W), Dallas, Texas, and concurrently to NMED
within 24 hours from the time the permittee becomes aware of the violation followed by a
written report in five days.

   None
candidates.computation_change_reason: This passage ties daily maximum limitation violations to a pollutant list that reads 'None' and points to Part III.D.7.b.(3) for operative detail. Interpreting whether 'None' means no daily-max limits exist, no pollutants trigger 24-hour oral reporting, or limits are defined only in the cross-referenced Part III section could change which daily-max limits Purpose A treats as applicable and whether Purpose B treats 24-hour violation reporting as required for any pollutant.

candidates.exact_span: D. WHOLE EFFLUENT TOXICITY TESTING (7 DAY CHRONIC NOEC)
candidates.computation_change_reason: The heading characterizes the obligation as 7-day chronic NOEC whole-effluent toxicity testing rather than conventional numeric effluent concentration limits. A different reading of whether NOEC-based WET results constitute enforceable numeric discharge limits versus separate toxicity-monitoring requirements would change Purpose A limit-applicability classification and Purpose B monitoring-applicability scope.

candidates.exact_span: Once initiated, all toxicity tests must be completed unless specific authority has been granted by EPA Region 6 or the State NPDES permitting authority.
candidates.computation_change_reason: This conditions when an initiated toxicity test may be treated as legitimately incomplete. Interpreting whether a partial or terminated WET test counts as missing required evidence, a documented no-data state with authority, or an unresolved case would change Purpose C missing-evidence classification.

candidates.exact_span: The permittee shall test the effluent for toxicity in accordance with the provisions in this section.
candidates.computation_change_reason: This is the operative monitoring mandate for WET. Whether this obligation applies to a given facility, outfall, and period determines Purpose B applicability, and whether absent WET results represent required-but-unreported monitoring versus another no-data state drives Purpose C semantics.

This scopes WET requirements to final outfall 001. Interpreting which discharge points fall within 'final outfall(s) 001' changes which outfalls Purpose B evaluates for WET obligations and which discharge points Purpose A associates with any WET-derived compliance criteria tied to this section.

Critical dilution defines the effluent concentration at which WET pass/fail is judged. A different interpretation of the 100% value or how it is applied to reported NOEC data would change whether Purpose A finds an exceedance of the applicable WET criterion.

The dilution series specifies the test concentrations used to derive NOEC compliance outcomes. Interpreting which series values are mandatory, how rounding or interpolation is handled, or whether the listed percentages govern pass/fail would change Purpose A compliance comparison results for WET.

candidates.exact_span: SAMPLE TYPE                        Defined in PART I
candidates.computation_change_reason: Sample type is not defined in this segment and is deferred to PART I. Without resolving that cross-reference, interpretation of whether grab versus composite or other sample types were required—and whether missing results reflect unmet sampling obligations—remains uncertain, changing Purpose B applicability and Purpose C missing-evidence categorization.
